Deal Structure Targets Major Production Expansion

Rodriguez on state broadcaster VTV said, “This 25-year bilateral project envisages the development of 17 strategic oilfields.” “That figure relates solely to the bilateral agreement between Venezuela and the United States.”
The comments from the interim president follow President
Donald Trump

‘s announcement Friday that the U.S. secured majority control of over 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan reserves through a private-sector partnership, aiming to boost crude supply and ease U.S. fuel prices.
Revenue Projections

Rodriguez said the broader plan also includes eight greenfield oil blocks, with Venezuela currently pumping about 1.25 million bpd. Notably, Venezuela has the world’s largest proven oil reserves, but its production remains far below its potential due to years of underinvestment, mismanagement and sanctions.

Rodríguez estimated the agreement could generate about $209 billion in revenue for Venezuela over its 25-year term, based on a $65-per-barrel benchmark, with roughly $19 per barrel flowing directly to the state.

Rodriguez also said that the country retained “ownership of and sovereignty” over its natural resources, “while leveraging capital, technology and operational expertise to support the recovery of a strategic industry that has been severely affected by sanctions.”
